capitals.name: Brunei Town, Kampong Ayer (now Bandar Seri Begawan)

ledger.x: 1363: the Sultanate of Brunei at Kota Batu.

c. 1492: the coast of north-west Borneo is Brunei's. 'the sultanate controlled the coastal areas of northwest Borneo' under Bolkiah (reign 1485-1524); the page dates no step inside the reign, so 1492 is Cliopatria's year. No state is named on the coast.

c. 1502: the Borneo coast widens inland and along Sabah. The Bolkiah page gives Bolkiah 'essentially all of coastal Borneo' and rule 'as far south as Banjarmasin' without years; only the north-west part is kept.

c. 1507: Sulu under Brunei's sphere. 'Defeated the states of Suluk and Seludang' and 'Manila and the Sulu Archipelago' in his dominion, undated; Bolkiah also married the daughter of the Sulu sultan. The year is Cliopatria's. A tint, not…
1578: Sulu is free.
April 1578: the Spanish take Brunei Town.
26 June 1578: the Spanish leave.
1619: three cells to Sambas.
c. 1629: north Palawan passes to Spain. No page opened dates Spain's Palawan posts or Brunei's hold on Palawan.

c. 1660: the capital moves from Kota Batu to Brunei Town on the water village of Kampong Ayer (infobox: 'Kota Batu (1368-1660)', 'Brunei Town, Kampong Ayer (1660-1920)'); the page links the end of the old capital to the civil war.
1673: eastern Sabah to Sulu, at the end of the civil war (1661-1673).
24 September 1841: Brunei grants Sarawak to James Brooke.
c. 1842: Palawan passes to Spain. Page silent on Palawan.
1846: Labuan to Britain.
1852: Saribas and Skrang to Brooke.
1861: the Rajang River basin to Brooke.
c. 1868: four more Sarawak cells.

c. 1870: the rest of the Sarawak coast between the Rajang and the Baram to Brooke. The Rajang basin part is the page's 1861; Bintulu, Mukah, Baram are undated on the pages opened (a gap-filler should open the Baram and Bintulu articles).
1877: the Sabah coast leased to the North Borneo company.
May 1884: the Putatan River ceded.
November 1884: the Padas district ceded.
November 1884: the lease of 1877 ends in cession, the Sabah coast being the company's.
1885: Trusan to Sarawak.
17 September 1888: Brunei becomes a British protectorate.
17 March 1890: Limbang annexed.
December 1941: the Japanese occupy Brunei.
June 1945: Brunei is liberated.
1 January 1984: independence.

wars.name: Castilian War
wars.outcome: The Spanish took Sulu and in April 1578 captured Brunei Town; driven out after 72 days (back in Manila on 26 June 1578).

wars.name: Bruneian Civil War of 1660
wars.outcome: Muhyiddin defeated and killed Abdul Hakkul Mubin; Sulu says it helped and was promised eastern Sabah, a claim that persists.

wars.name: Brooke's conflict with the Sultan
wars.outcome: 'In 1843, an open conflict between Brooke and the Sultan ended in the latter's defeat.'

wars.name: Limbang annexation
wars.outcome: Charles Brooke annexed Limbang on 17 March 1890; the British decided in August 1892 that Sarawak should keep it; the case was 'considered closed' in August 1895 without agreement.

certainty.note: A coastal and riverine sultanate: no surveyed boundary; the Sarawak and Sabah frontiers are cessions of districts and river basins without lines.
The cessions of 1884-1885, the decision on Limbang in 1892 and the protectorate fix the Sarawak and Sabah frontiers on paper; Limbang was never agreed by the Sultan (1895).
